chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ash-Shah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamid narrated to us, saying: Abu Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Salih al-Tamimy narrated to us, on the authority of his father, saying: Anas ibn Muhammad ibn Abu Malik narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them), from the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)...

...that he said in his will to him: 'O Ali! A single dirham spent for dye is better than one thousand dirhams spent in the cause of Allah. And in it are fourteen characteristics: It expels wind from the ears, it clarifies the sight, it softens the nostrils, it improves the scent/flavor, it strengthens the gums, it eliminates weakness/decay, it reduces the whispering of Satan, the angels rejoice in it, the believer takes glad tidings from it, it enrages the disbeliever, it is an ornament and a perfume, the questioning angels (Munkar and Nakir) feel shy of it, and it constitutes innocence/pardon for him in his grave.'

key_terms.الضَّنَى: Weakness or decay (often referring to eyes or general vitality)
key_terms.الْخَضَابُ: Dyeing (hair/beard), specifically using kohl or henna
key_terms.دِرْهَمٌ: A dirham, a unit of currency
key_terms.مَنْكَرٌ وَنَكِيرٌ: The two angels who question the deceased in the grave

ai.seo_question: What are the fourteen spiritual and physical benefits of using kohl or dye according to the Prophet's will to Ali?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from the Ahl al-Bayt chain, highlighting the Prophet’s specific emphasis on personal grooming as an act of worship (*ibadah*) and sunnah. The comparison of a single dirham for dye to a thousand in general charity underscores the unique spiritual merit of maintaining one’s appearance for prayer and social dignity, linking physical cleanliness to spiritual purity. This tradition reflects the Shia emphasis on the Prophet’s practical instructions to Ali as the inheritor of his sunnah, where mundane acts carry eschatological weight.
